text:
maya: heads-up — we started seeing a perf regression in TP all-reduce on the 48KB-ish message size range after the kernel-selector change yesterday. latency +20-35% on pipeline steps that do reduce-scatter + all-gather.

alex: can you paste the repro command? is this on the nightly model or the canary runtime?

maya: nightly runtime (build 2026-03-17), test config: `--tp=2 --pp=1 --micro-batch=4 --seq=2048`. repro script: `./run_tp_perf.sh --model t5x-small --scale 8 --msgsize-target 48k`.

jeff: I saw something similar locally. nvprof trace shows lots of small NCCL ops with an extra kernel-selection syscall between ReduceScatter and the local kernel — looks like we fall back to the tree algo for some chunks and ring for others. cc @liang for kernel selector heuristics.

liang: that matches the selector change: we now choose tree when (msgsize < 64KB && comm_shape == many_small_chunks). The intent was to reduce latency for tiny messages but we may be thrashing when chunk boundaries align badly with our kv-cache flush windows.

maya: attaching short perf snippet from perfbot:
```
perfbot: trace summary (tp_step=187)
  reduce-scatter: 12.3ms (ring), 18.9ms (tree)  <-- 3/8 ranks used tree here
  local-apply: 4.1ms
  all-gather: 9.7ms (ring), 14.5ms (tree)
  kernel-switch overhead: ~1.8ms/call when selector flips
  kv-cache spill events: 6 spikes at same step (kv-cache eviction triggered)
```

alex: kernel-switch overhead 1.8ms is big. is that the selector doing a launch+sync or are we JIT-recompiling kernels?

liang: it's the kernel switch syscall path: we rebind buffers, adjust launch params, and call into the new NCCL plan creation when algorithm differs. That path had a rare lock contended after the selector change. I can reproduce a 1.5-2ms hitch if selector flips mid-iteration.

jeff: quick experiment idea — pin selector to always ring for the test and see if latency stabilizes. if so, we know the algo mix is the issue rather than bandwidth.

maya: ran pinned-ring run: latency down to baseline, no kv-cache spills, much lower variance.

liang: ok that's helpful. hypothesis: when chunk boundaries align to KV cache eviction, we end up splitting a message so half uses tree and half uses ring (or vice versa), causing extra NCCL handshake + our selector rebind. Also KV cache eviction increases memory pressure, changing kernel launch params and triggering selector retries.

alex: curious — does batching heuristics (micro-batch grouping) influence chunk alignment? if we coalesce tokens differently we might avoid the boundary.

maya: yes — increasing micro-batch to 8 shifts chunk boundaries; the regression goes away but that isn't a fix for production. we need selector resilience or consistent algo choice.

jeff: low-risk mitigation: add sticky-algo per-iteration (choose ring or tree at the start of the step based on median msgsize) to avoid flipping mid-step. Liang, can you prototype?

liang: will try a sticky-algo flag `--algo-sticky=true` that forces one plan per step. also will gate the slow path with a trylock so we don't block Hot threads if selector wants to rebind.

perfbot: FYI — created perf ticket PERF-3197 with traces and nvprof tarball.

maya: noted. next steps: (1) liang to prototype sticky-algo + trylock, (2) jeff to run end-to-end perf with sticky on nightly, (3) maya to validate kv-cache metrics and check eviction thresholds are sane.

alex: also add a short unit test: simulate alternating msgsize that would cause flip, assert no >1ms selector hitch per step. keep it small.

liang: prototype pushed to branch `tp/sticky-algo-trylock` (still WIP). early numbers: selector hitch drops to ~0.2ms, overall TP step latency within 3% baseline.

maya: awesome. thx all. we'll leave ring pinned in prod for the affected customers until we merge sticky-algo. :thumbsup:

jeff: one more note — add telemetry for "algo-flips-per-step" and kv-cache eviction correlation so we can detect this automatically in console dashboards.

maya: filed ENG-TP-eviction-alert item. closing thread once sticky patch is in canary.

perfbot: deploy-bot: canary runtime build queued (id=canary-2026-03-18-07).
